entries.title: Bounded iid lattice FPP and deterministic cylinder restriction
entries.statement: On undirected nearest-neighbor Z^d, d>=2, assign iid Uniform[1,2] weights. T(x,y) is the minimum total weight over paths from x to y. For an induced finite box C containing a straight n-edge route from x to x+n e_1, T_C is the analogous constrained minimum. The unique unrestricted geodesic exists almost surely. Its deviation D(x,y) is the maximum Euclidean distance from the segment [x,y]. Along these axis endpoints n<=T<=T_C<=2n, and T_C-T vanishes whenever the geodesic is contained in C.

entries.title: A uniform variance floor from the origin edges
entries.statement: For iid Uniform[1,2] undirected nearest-neighbor FPP on Z^d, d>=2, Var T(0,v)>=4^{-(4d+1)} for every nonzero lattice v. A minimizing path exists, is unique almost surely, and has at most 2||v||_1 edges. This only certifies the nonnegative lower fluctuation threshold; it does not prove a positive exponent or exponent equality.
entries.proof_text: A coordinate path costs <=2||v||_1; positivity confines all possible minimizing paths to a finite ball and bounds their lengths. Continuous independent weights rule out distinct-path ties. Condition on the exterior of the 2d origin edges. T=min_i(U_i+A_i), where A_i are exterior-measurable route costs avoiding the origin. When all U_i<=5/4, T<=min A_i+5/4; when all U_i>=7/4, T>=min A_i+7/4. Each event has conditional probability 4^{-2d}. Two independent conditional copies and Var X=(1/2)E(X-X')^2 give conditional variance >=4^{-4d}/4. Total variance proves the bound.

entries.title: Variance transfer through nonnegative coupling errors
entries.statement: Let F_1,F_2 be identically distributed square-integrable variables with standard deviation s, and G_1,G_2 iid square-integrable variables on the same probability space. Suppose Delta_i=G_i-F_i>=0 have equal means and ||Delta_i||_2<=delta. Then 2(s-2delta)_+^2<=Var(F_1-F_2)<=2(s+2delta)^2. Independence is required only for G_1,G_2, and is not assumed for localization events, errors, or F_1,F_2.
entries.proof_text: Centering contracts L2, so |sd G_i-s|<=delta. Positivity gives E(Delta_1-Delta_2)^2<=E Delta_1^2+E Delta_2^2<=2delta^2. Both passage-time differences have mean zero; independence gives ||G_1-G_2||_2=sqrt(2)sd G_1. Apply the forward and reverse L2 triangle inequalities, then square.
assumptions: identical F marginals and identical G marginals
nonnegative errors with equal means and the stated L2 bound

entries.title: A sufficient polynomial confinement budget for variance decoupling
entries.statement: Consider two translated axis passage times F_i=T(x_i,x_i+n e_1) in iid Uniform[1,2] undirected FPP, restricted times G_i in translated induced boxes with disjoint deterministic edge sets and containing the straight n-edge routes. If sd F_i>=c n^b and the probability that F_i differs from G_i is <=C n^{-q}, for all sufficiently large n, then q>2(1-b) implies Var(F_1-F_2)/(2Var F_1)->1. Departure of the unique geodesic is a sufficient exceptional event. This is conditional and does not establish confinement.
entries.proof_text: The constrained times are iid because they depend on disjoint deterministic coordinates. For Delta_i=G_i-F_i, 0<=Delta_i<=n and Delta_i=0 off the exceptional event, so ||Delta_i||_2<=n sqrt(p_n). Divide the nonnegative-coupling variance inequalities by 2s_n^2. Their error ratio is at most (sqrt(C)/c)n^{1-q/2-b}, which tends to zero.
assumptions: translated boxes with disjoint edge sets
straight axis route contained in each box
c>0, C<infinity and the two stated bounds for all large n

entries.title: Positive mean gaps give a dependence-safe departure bound
entries.statement: For iid Uniform[1,2] undirected FPP on Z^d, let m(x)=ET(0,x), v=n e_1, and C=([-w,n+w] x [-w,w]^{d-1}) intersect Z^d, with n,w positive integers. Assume a>=0, alpha>0, M<infinity and E exp(alpha|T(0,x)-m(x)|/|x|^a)<=M for every nonzero lattice x. If m(z)+m(v-z)-m(v)>=H_n>0 for every z in the l1 ball of radius 2n outside C, then P(the 0-to-v geodesic leaves C)<=3M(4n+1)^d exp(-alpha H_n/[3(3n)^a]). No independence among the three passage times is needed. The positive mean-gap assumption is not proved for this law here.
entries.proof_text: A departing geodesic visits one of at most (4n+1)^d deterministic candidate vertices z. At that vertex T(0,v)=T(0,z)+T(z,v). Subtract means: at least one of the three absolute centered fluctuations is >=H_n/3. Their endpoint distances are <=3n. Exponential Markov, translation invariance and a union bound over three events and the deterministic vertex set give the displayed bound.
assumptions: the stated iid bounded FPP model
positive deterministic mean-gap bound on the stated finite vertex set

entries.title: Short endpoints obstruct a literal all-endpoint wandering lower bound
entries.statement: For iid Uniform[1,2] undirected FPP on Z^d, d>=2, D(0,e_1)=0 for every environment and D(0,2e_1)=0 almost surely. Therefore inf_{v!=0} ED(0,v)/|v|^b=0 for every real b. A lower wandering exponent definition must allow a large-distance cutoff for this candidate. Chatterjee's original (A4) allows that cutoff; an all-nonzero-endpoint version cannot be applied literally to this law.
entries.proof_text: For e_1 the direct edge costs <=2 and alternatives have at least three edges, costing >=3. For 2e_1 the straight two-edge route costs <4 almost surely and every alternative has at least four edges, costing >=4. In both cases the geodesic follows the segment, so its deviation is zero.
assumptions: D measured from the endpoint segment

entries.title: Vanishing exceptional probability alone does not certify variance decoupling
entries.statement: For fixed 0<=b<1 and n>=2, take Z_n Bernoulli with p_n=n^{-2(1-b)}, F_1=F_2=n(2-Z_n), G_1=G_2=2n. The G_i are independent constants, n<=F_i<=G_i<=2n, the errors are nonnegative and <=n, and F_i=G_i except on probability p_n->0. Nevertheless Var F_i=n^{2b}(1-p_n) and Var(F_1-F_2)=0. This refutes the abstract inference from vanishing departure probability to decoupling; it is not an iid FPP construction or a KPZ counterexample.
entries.proof_text: Both F_i are the same Bernoulli function, so their difference is identically zero. Constant G_i are independent, and G_i-F_i=n Z_n. Direct Bernoulli moments yield Var F_i=n^2 p_n(1-p_n)=n^{2b}(1-p_n).

entries.title: P0110: unproved global exponent coincidence and local mean-gap input
entries.statement: P0110 asks for one nondegenerate iid undirected lattice FPP law for which the KPZ relation chi=2xi-1 is proved with suitable exponents. For the Uniform[1,2] candidate, the parent input remains UNPROVED: chi_a=chi_b and xi_a=xi_b in Chatterjee's original definitions. Upper thresholds use uniform exponential moments of |T-ET|/|v|^a and D/|v|^a over all nonzero lattice endpoints; lower thresholds use uniform lower powers for Var T and ED over all sufficiently distant lattice endpoints. The local cylinder route additionally lacks a positive mean-gap bound m(z)+m(ne_1-z)-m(ne_1)>=c w^2/n at some sublinear width w. The verified coupling and union-bound reductions prove neither input. relations.rationale: The variance floor uses the iid Uniform[1,2] origin edges and unrestricted passage time defined in setup.
The budget substitutes delta=n sqrt(p_n) and s_n>=c n^b into the displayed variance-transfer inequalities.
The axis-route bound n<=T<=T_C<=2n supplies the n-sized nonnegative error.
Positive weights confine the unrestricted minimizing path to the deterministic l1 ball and identify a departing vertex.
Weights between one and two force the short axis geodesics to be straight.
At q=2(1-b) the counterexample has individual variance of order n^{2b} and zero difference variance, showing why the budget cannot be replaced by p_n->0 for arbitrary couplings.
The gap card explicitly names the unproved positive mean-gap assumption of this conditional departure lemma and distinguishes it from global exponent equality.
